reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The graph shows the heights of four girls.

[Image: Bar graph showing heights of four girls]

The names are missing from the graph. Debbie is the tallest. Amy is the shortest. Dawn is taller than Sarah. How tall is Sarah?
reference_items.figure_description:
A vertical bar graph titled "Names of Girls" along the horizontal axis, and labeled "Height (Centimeters)" along the vertical axis.
The vertical axis has tick marks from 0 to 150 in increments of 25 (0, 25, 50, 75, 100, 125, 150).
There are four unlabeled shaded bars from left to right:
- The first bar has a height of 100.
- The second bar has a height of 150.
- The third bar has a height of 125.
- The fourth bar has a height of 75.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
The graph shows 500 cedar trees and 150 hemlock trees.

[Image: Pictograph of trees]

How many trees does each [Image: Tree] represent?

Answer: ____

A pictograph table with two rows and two columns:
- Top row: labeled "Cedar" on the left; on the right are 5 identical full evergreen tree symbols in a horizontal line.
- Bottom row: labeled "Hemlock" on the left; on the right is 1 full evergreen tree symbol followed by half of an evergreen tree symbol (vertically cut, showing only the left half).
Below the table, the question includes an inline image of a single full evergreen tree symbol between the words "each" and "represent?".

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: a piece of string curved both ends and a rule in cm with value from 1 to 10.]

If the string in the diagram above is pulled straight, which of these is closest to its length?
reference_items.figure_description:
A metric ruler and a folded piece of string above it. The ruler has major tick marks labeled from 1 to 10 with "cm" before the 1, and intermediate half-centimeter tick marks between each number.

The string is laid horizontally above the ruler with both ends folded back:
- The bottom-left end starts at the 4 cm mark and extends left to the 3 cm mark, where it loops around 180 degrees.
- The middle section runs continuously to the right from the 3 cm mark to approximately the 8 cm mark.
- At approximately the 8 cm mark, it loops around 180 degrees upward and extends back to the left, ending at approximately the 6.5 cm mark.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
This table shows the ages of the girls and boys in a club.

| Age | Number of Girls | Number of Boys |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | 4 | 6 |
| 9 | 8 | 4 |
| 10 | 6 | 10 |

Use the information in the table to complete the graph for ages 9 and 10.

[Image: Double bar graph]

descriptors: All 4 bars correct for height, placement, and shading.
All 4 bars of correct height; either bars misplaced or bars shaded incorrectly in no more than one set (i.e., for age 9 or age 10).
Placement, shading, and height all correct for one, two, or three bars. (At least one bar completely correct).
All 4 bars of correct height, but two or more errors involving placement or shading.
Work is shown, but no bars are drawn. For example: only numbers are shown on the graph.

reference_items.figure_description: An incomplete double bar graph. The vertical axis is labeled "Number" with tick marks and horizontal grid lines at 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. The horizontal axis is labeled "Age" with positions for 8, 9, and 10. A legend in the upper right shows a dark grey shaded square labeled "Girls" and an unshaded (white) square labeled "Boys". For age 8, two bars are plotted: a grey shaded bar of height 4 (Girls) followed by an adjacent white unshaded bar of height 6 (Boys). For ages 9 and 10, no bars are drawn.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
